sections.label: Philosophy
sections.title: The Architecture of Possibilities
sections.body: We do not design jewellery; we construct architectural narratives sealed in silver and bronze within the physical realm. Silver & Elegant was founded on the belief that the most enduring objects are those calculated with high mathematical intelligence and crafted with immense discipline. Each piece is a "Future Heirloom"—complex enough to be computed algorithmically, yet durable enough to outlive its creator. By distancing ourselves from the reflexes of fast consumption and transient trends, we establish permanence as our definitive design standard.

sections.label: Process
sections.title: Code and Hammer
sections.body: Every design begins not with a sketch, but with a structural problem: What form should permanence take? We utilise generative design algorithms as our creative partners. Our code and simulations analyse thousands of structural possibilities simultaneously, allowing us to discover geometric forms of a complexity unattainable by the human hand alone. To bring this rational architecture into the physical world, we must refine it through traditional craftsmanship. Shaped by the hands of a master using the lost-wax casting technique, the metals bear the marks of human soul and imperfection, contrasting against digital precision. What the code proposes, the hand shapes. What the hand creates, time preserves.

sections.label: Creator
sections.title: A Union of Two Worlds
sections.body: I am Esen Tunalı Sarı. The vision behind Silver & Elegant was forged in the historic jewellery quarters of Istanbul, where my childhood unfolded. As the child of a family that migrated from Bulgaria, I grew up amidst masters of silver and diamond setting, where craftsmanship was not merely a technique, but a daily discipline of life. The software engineering background I acquired years later allowed me to merge this traditional craft with the millimetric precision of algorithms. Today, in our home studio in Borehamwood, London, we melt these two opposing worlds into a single language. We do not manufacture like a factory, nor do we hide solely in the past; we bring together the intelligence of technology and the heart of craftsmanship.

process_steps.title: Sketch
process_steps.description: Each piece begins as a drawing — a study of form, proportion, and intention before a single tool is picked up.

process_steps.title: Form
process_steps.description: Sterling silver sheet or wire is cut, shaped, and worked by hand. No two sessions produce the same result — the material makes its own decisions.

process_steps.title: Finish
process_steps.description: The surface is treated to reveal its character — polished, oxidised, or left with the texture of the hammer. Nothing is erased.

articles.title: NOT JUST A LABEL — 'Black Sheep' Selection: Pioneers of Independent Design
articles.content: Our design house has been honoured with the 'Black Sheep' status by NOT JUST A LABEL (NJAL), one of the world's most significant authorities on independent fashion. Being showcased on NJAL’s global homepage as a brand with a pioneering vision marks a foundational turning point for Silver & Elegant. This selection—which rejects categorisation, pushes the boundaries of independent fashion, and advocates for ethical production—affirms our commitment to standing at the intersection of architectural innovation and enduring craftsmanship.

articles.title: PAUL COSTELLOE AW26 — London Fashion Week (The Waldorf Hilton, London): Wearable Art on the Runway
articles.content: We were proud to be one of the official jewellery partners for the Paul Costelloe Autumn/Winter 2026 collection, the debut show under William Costelloe’s creative direction at London Fashion Week. Hosted in the enchanting atmosphere of The Waldorf Hilton, our pieces were integrated into the runway through the meticulous curation of the creative team and stylist Borna Prikaski. This partnership served as a powerful expression of our traditional craft heritage and experimental architectural lines on the high-fashion stage.

articles.title: BOREHAMWOOD TIMES: From Local Roots to the London Fashion Week Runway
articles.content: Our journey, stretching from local roots to global runways, was featured in the editorial pages of the Borehamwood Times. The article documents our design methodology—spanning from traditional silversmithing disciplines to the mathematical precision of software code—and our brand’s debut on the London Fashion Week opening show stage within its first year.

articles.title: FLANELLE MAGAZINE: The Interaction of Shadow and Metal
articles.content: Our hand-crafted silver and bronze structures were featured in an editorial for the prestigious avant-garde fashion publication, Flanelle Magazine. The shoot highlights the sharp geometry and the interaction between shadow and metallic surfaces inherent in our designs. Photography: Izabela Wojnarowska | Styling: Tia Oguri | Hair & Makeup: Karoliina Villem | Retouch: Daria Sheyanova | Model: Yitian Lu | Hair Design: Anne Veck

articles.title: KALTBLUT MAGAZINE — "THE DISH": Contemporary Jewellery Engineering and Avant-Garde Creative Direction
articles.content: Silver & Elegant designs were curated for "THE DISH," a digital editorial exploring the boundaries of contemporary jewellery engineering and avant-garde creative direction. Published in KALTBLUT Magazine, this exclusive selection emphasises the sculptural posture and structural strength of jewellery on the body. Creative Team: Doma Dovgialo, Borna Prikaski, Yassine V.K, Ambra Castelli, Giulia Oldani, Tobia Bartolini, Christina Lomas, Scarlett Leatham, Shyy Sachdev. Featured Brands: Alice Skewis Jewellery, Capsule Eleven, Vicki Sarge, Silver & Elegant, Annabel B. Jewellery.

pieces.name: Crustacea I Earrings
pieces.tagline: Untamed opulence, hand-sculpted for a commanding presence.
pieces.story:
A bold, sculptural tribute to resilience and raw organic form, Crustacea I captures the untamed opulence of the deep. Each piece is meticulously pavé-set with brilliant crystals that trace a powerful, fluid anatomy, accented by striking ruby-red and onyx-black stones. Hand-sculpted in architectural bronze and finished with a 22K gold lustre, they seamlessly blend high-fashion maximalism with refined artisanal depth.

Handcrafted via the traditional lost-wax technique by a single master artisan, these limited-edition artefacts balance a commanding weight with engineered comfort, finished with hypoallergenic silver posts. The subtle surface variations are intentional signatures of the maker, serving as tangible proof of a human touch in a machine-made age.

pieces.name: Reptilia I Earrings
pieces.tagline: Primordial power reframed into a modern masterpiece of wearable art.
pieces.story:
An Online Exclusive. A powerful tribute to strength, endurance, and ancient symbolism, Reptilia I captures the primordial power of its namesake through bold, architectural lines. Each piece is hand-shaped in textured bronze and enveloped in a radiant, heavy layer of 22K gold lustre, transforming a raw organic form into a sophisticated statement of modern luxury.

True to our philosophy of transparent craft, these limited-edition artefacts balance an assertive, commanding scale with an engineered, weightless comfort. Finished with hypoallergenic sterling silver posts, the deliberate surface textures remain as the proud signature of the master artisan—serving as tangible proof of a human touch in a machine-made age.

Accented by the soft, warm glow of natural peach gemstones, the design masterfully balances structural geometry with organic warmth. Hand-sculpted in architectural bronze and finished with a rich 22K gold lustre, they serve as a quietly powerful statement for the discerning collector.

Handcrafted via the traditional lost-wax technique by a single master artisan, these limited-edition artefacts balance a bold, graphic silhouette with engineered, weightless comfort. Reflecting our commitment to transparent craft, the organic surface textures remain as intentional signatures of the maker—tangible proof of a human touch in a machine-made age.

pieces.name: Stepped Bevel Studs
pieces.tagline: Brutalist architecture translated into geometric sterling gold and crystal studs.
pieces.story:
Inspired by Brutalist architecture, these studs serve as geometric skeletons. The stepped bronze frame, enveloped in a rich 22K gold lustre, echoes the monumental ceilings of ancient sanctuaries. At its core, a brilliant clear crystal captures the light, contrasting with the deep shadows of the hand-carved metal.

Handcrafted via the ancient lost-wax technique by a single master artisan, they bridge the gap between generative precision and the organic warmth of human touch.

pieces.name: Shadowed Bevel Studs
pieces.tagline: Smoky quartz suspended in stepped architectural bronze frames.
pieces.story:
The enigmatic twin to our Bevel series, these studs pair warm-toned architectural bronze with the smoky, deep shadows of natural quartz. Light is not meant to reflect here, but to be absorbed into the depths of the smoky stone, creating a quiet, atmospheric play of shadow.

Conceptualised as future heirlooms, each pair features unique natural inclusions in the quartz, ensuring a bespoke micro-architecture for its keeper.

Drawing inspiration from the hidden fractals of the deep sea, these studs merge the organic symmetry of the starfish with celestial alignments. Each marquise-cut crystal is set to mimic the algorithmic scattering of light beneath the waves, contrasting beautifully with the raw strength of the bronze base.

These are not mere accessories, but wearable artefacts carrying the silent geometry of the ocean and the cosmos.

pieces.tagline: Mythological horse heads with emerald eyes and suspended golden spheres.

The organic surface marks are intentional signatures of the maker, a testament to authentic craftsmanship in a machine-made age.

pieces.name: Baroque Chelonia Earrings
pieces.tagline: Computational turtle shells and natural baroque pearls in gold lattice.
pieces.story:
A celebration of nature's slowest, most patient creations: the evolutionary geometry of the turtle shell and the organic growth of the baroque pearl. The turquoise-toned body is enveloped in a gold lattice, generated computationally to simulate natural shell structures.

Dangling below, asymmetric baroque pearls introduce nature's beautiful imperfections—no two pearls are alike, making your pair entirely bespoke.

An elegant, high-fashion testament to the cycle of time and structural permanence.
